title: scram-auth — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins the byte-level contract for the Phase 2 sync-server authentication mechanism SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS (MYND-420; RFC 7677/5802 + RFC 9266 tls-exporter channel binding; spec docs/spec/server-protocol.md auth section). The authenticated secret is the high-entropy HKDF(root_key,'server-auth') value, so iteration count is minimal. Each case pins: the server-stored verifier (StoredKey = SHA-256(ClientKey); ServerKey = HMAC(SaltedPassword,'Server Key'); SaltedPassword = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256(secret, salt, i)), the client proof (ClientKey XOR HMAC(StoredKey, AuthMessage)), and the server signature (HMAC(ServerKey, AuthMessage)) — where the AuthMessage incorporates the channel-binding input (gs2-header || cbind_data). Changing cbind_data with the same secret/salt yields the same verifier but a different proof, proving channel binding is load-bearing. NOTE: these golden vectors are generated from the Go server reference implementation (myne-server/internal/auth/scram); the Rust client must reproduce them byte-exact — that cross-impl parity is gated by the MYND-420 R3 primitive-level review.

input_iterations.description: PBKDF2 iteration count (1 for a 256-bit secret).
